rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘from your women’ modifies stepdaughters: a stepdaughter whose mother the man has entered is forbidden, while one whose mother he has not entered is lawful.
rows.anchor: متعلق بربائبكم ومعناه أن الربيبة من المرأة المدخول بها محرمة على الرجل حلال له اذا لم يدخل بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attaching ‘from your women’ to both mothers-in-law and stepdaughters would make ‘from’ mean specification for the former but derivation for the latter, an impermissible shift within one expression.
rows.anchor: فقد جعلت ( من ) لبيان النساء وتمييز المدخول بهن من غير المدخول بهن واذا قلت وربائبكم من نسائكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attaching the phrase only to mothers-in-law would leave the stepdaughter restriction ambiguous; the nearer phrase normally governs unless an obstacle intervenes.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز الثاني لأن ما يليه هو الذي يستوجب التعليق به ما لم يعترض أمر لا يرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible alternative is to attach it to both women and stepdaughters, taking ‘from’ to express connection.
rows.anchor: الا ان تقول اعلقه بالنساء والربائب وأجعل ( من ) للاتصال كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sense of connection is illustrated by ‘the hypocrite men and women are of one another’; mothers-in-law connect to wives as mothers, and stepdaughters to their mothers as daughters.
rows.anchor: ﴿ المنافقون والمنافقات بعضهم من بعض ﴾ التوبة 67 فإني لست منك ولست مني ما انا من دد ولا الدد مني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars agree that the prohibition of mothers-in-law is unconditional, unlike the stepdaughter prohibition, following the apparent wording of the verse.
rows.anchor: اتفقوا على أن تحريم امهات النساء مبهم دون تحريم الربائب على ما عليه ظاهر كلام الله تعالى

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says a man who divorced his wife before consummation may marry her daughter but may not marry her mother.
rows.anchor: وقد روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في رجل تزوج امراة ثم طلقها قبل ان يدخل بها انه قال ( لا بأس ان يتزوج ابنتها

rows.speaker: عمر وعمران بن الحصين
rows.claim: They held that a mother-in-law becomes forbidden as soon as the marriage contract is made.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر وعمران بن الحصين رضي الله عنهما ان الأم تحرم بنفس العقد

rows.speaker: مسروق
rows.claim: Masruq said the mother-in-law prohibition is unrestricted, so people should leave unrestricted what God left unrestricted.
rows.anchor: وعن مسروق هي مرسلة فأرسلوا ما أرسل الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas likewise urged leaving ambiguous what God left ambiguous.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أبهموا ما أبهم الله

rows.speaker: علي وابن عباس وزيد وابن عمر وابن الزبير
rows.claim: These authorities are reported to have read ‘and your wives’ mothers who have entered them’; Ibn Abbas swore that this was the revealed wording.
rows.anchor: الا ما روي عن علي وابن عباس وزيد وابن عمر وابن الزبير انهم قرءوا ( وأمهات نسائكم اللاتي دخلتم بهن )

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Two different reports are transmitted from Jabir on this question.
rows.anchor: وعن جابر روايتان وعن سعيد بن المسيب عن زيد

rows.speaker: زيد
rows.claim: Zayd, transmitted by Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib, disliked a man marrying his deceased wife’s mother if he inherited from her; divorce before consummation left the choice open, since death substitutes for consummation here as it does for dowry.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن المسيب عن زيد اذا ماتت عنده فأخذ ميراثها كره ان يخلف على امها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wife’s child by another man is called rabīb/rabība because a stepfather generally raises the child as he raises his own; the term later broadened to children he did not raise.
rows.anchor: وسمى ولد المرأة من غير زوجها ربيبا وربيبة لأنه يربهما كما يرب ولده في غالب الأمر ثم اتسع فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘In your care’ explains the prohibition: after consummation, marriage creates intimacy and affection that ordinarily lead a man to treat his wife’s children as his own.
rows.anchor: فائدته التعليل للتحريم وانهن لاحتضانكم لهن أو لكونهن بصدد احتضانكم وفي حكم التقلب في حجوركم

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali required a stepdaughter to be in the man’s care for the prohibition to apply; Dawud adopted this view.
rows.anchor: وعن على رضي الله عنه انه شرط ذلك في التحريم وبه اخذ داود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Entered upon them’ is a euphemism for intercourse, like saying that a man built over a woman or drew the curtain over her.
rows.anchor: ﴿ دخلتم بهن ﴾ قلت هي كناية عن الجماع كقولهم بني عليها وضرب عليها الحجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition is causative; Abu Hanifa treats touching and similar contact as taking the place of consummation.
rows.anchor: والباء للتعدية واللمس ونحوه يقوم مقام الدخول عند أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar ruled that a son could not marry a slave girl after Umar had secluded himself with her and stripped her, when the son asked for her.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر رضي الله عنه أنه خلا بجارية فجردها فاستوهبها ابن له فقال إنها لا تحل لك

rows.speaker: مسروق
rows.claim: Masruq ordered his slave girl sold after his death, saying he had touched and looked at her in ways that made her forbidden to his son.
rows.anchor: وعن مسروق أنه امر ان تباع جاريته بعد موته وقال اما إني لم اصب منها الا ما يحرمها على ولدي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan held that a man’s lustful squeezing, kissing, or uncovering of a slave woman makes her forbidden to his son in every case.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن في الرجل يملك الأمة فيغمزها لشهوة أو يقبلها أو يكشفها أنها لا تحل لولده بحال

rows.speaker: عطاء وحماد بن أبي سليمان
rows.claim: ʿAta and Hammad held that looking at a woman’s genitals prevents a man from marrying either her mother or daughter.
rows.anchor: وعن عطاء وحماد بن أبي سليمان اذا نظر إلى فرج امرأة فلا ينكح امها ولا بنتها

rows.speaker: الأوزاعي
rows.claim: Al-Awzaʿi held that entering the mother’s room, exposing her, touching her, closing the door, and lowering the curtain forbids marrying her daughter.
rows.anchor: وعن الأوزاعي اذا دخل بالأم فعراها ولمسها بيده وأغلق الباب وأرخى الستر فلا يحل له نكاح ابنتها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وطاوس وعمرو بن دينار
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Tawus, and Amr ibn Dinar held that the prohibition arises only from intercourse itself.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس وطاوس وعمرو بن دينار ان التحريم لا يقع الا بالجماع وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Of your loins’ excludes adopted sons; the Prophet married Zaynab bint Jahsh after Zayd ibn Haritha divorced her, as anticipated by the rule about adopted sons’ wives.
rows.anchor: وقد تزوج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم زينب بنت جحش الاسدية بنت عمته أميمة بنت عبد المطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘And that you combine’ is nominative, coordinated with the prohibited women, and prohibits combining two sisters in marriage.
rows.anchor: في موضع الرفع عطف على المحرمات أي وحرم عليكم الجمع بين الأختين والمراد حرمة النكاح

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali treated the prohibition of combining two sisters as applying to two women owned as slaves, since one verse permits them and another forbids them.
rows.anchor: فعن عثمان وعلي رضي الله عنهما أنهما قالا أحلتهما آية وحرمتهما آية يعنيان هذه الآية

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: Uthman resolved the conflict between the prohibition and the permission for two owned sisters in favor of permissibility.
rows.anchor: يعنيان هذه الآية وقوله ﴿ أو ما ملكت أيمانكم ﴾ النساء 3 فرجح على التحريم وعثمان التحليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception for what preceded means past conduct is forgiven, as confirmed by the following statement that God is forgiving and merciful.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إلا ما قد سلف ﴾ ولكن ما مضى مغفور بدليل قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The standard reading has fatḥa on the ṣād of muḥṣanāt; Talha’s kasra reading means women with husbands, since marriage has guarded their chastity.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والمحصنات ﴾ القراءة بفتح الصاد وعن طلحة بن مصرف انه قرأ بكسر الصاد وهن ذوات الأزواج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Married captive women from enemy territory become lawful to Muslim fighters despite their existing marriages; al-Farazdaq’s verse is cited as evidence.
rows.anchor: يريد ما ملكت أيمانهم من اللاتي سبين ولهن أزواج في دار الكفر فهن حلال لغزاة المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq’s line about a woman with a husband captured by Muslim lances is evidence that she is lawful to the man who takes her.
rows.anchor: وفي معناه قول الفرزدق ( وذات حليل أنكحتها رماحنا … حلال لمن يبني بها لم تطلق )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘God’s ordinance upon you’ is an emphatic verbal noun: God prescribed this as a binding obligation, namely the prohibitions just listed.
rows.anchor: ﴿ كتاب الله عليكم ﴾ مصدر مؤكد أي كتب الله ذلك عليكم كتابا وفرضه فرضا وهو تحريم ما حرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘And He has made lawful’ coordinates with an understood verb governing ‘God’s ordinance’; the Yamani reading ‘God prescribed’ supports this, while the passive reading coordinates with ‘were forbidden.’
rows.anchor: قلت على الفعل المضمر الذي نصب ﴿ كتاب الله ﴾ أي كتب الله عليكم تحريم ذلك واحل لكم ما وراء ذلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose of explaining what is lawful is that men seek it with their wealth while chaste, protecting themselves from forbidden sex; spending wealth on illicit relations brings worldly and religious loss.
rows.anchor: ارادة ان يكون ابتغاؤكم ﴿ بأموالكم ﴾ التى جعل الله لكم قياما في حال كونكم محصنين غير مسافحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iḥṣān means chastity and protecting oneself from forbidden conduct; wealth here means dowries and other marriage expenses.
rows.anchor: والإحصان العفة وتحصين النفس من الوقوع في الحرام والأموال المهور وما يخرج في المناكح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of ‘seek’ may be understood as women, but it is better left unexpressed, as if the wording simply meant spending money; alternatively, the phrase is an appositive of ‘beyond that.’
rows.anchor: يجوز ان يكون مقدرا وهو النساء والأجود ان لا يقدر وكانه قيل ان تخرجوا اموالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘That you seek’ may instead be parsed as an appositive to ‘beyond that’; musāfiḥ is an adulterer, from the image of semen pouring out, and the text preserves a vulgar phrase built on that root and madhy.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ﴿ أن تبتغوا ﴾ بدلا من ﴿ وراء ذلك ﴾ والمسافح الزاني من السفح وهو صب المني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enjoyment of a woman here means a wife with whom the man has intercourse, valid seclusion, or a marriage contract.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فما استمتعتم به منهن ﴾ فما استمتعتم به من المنكوحات من جماع أو خلوة صحيحة أو عقد عليهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypothetical commands recall the Israelites’ punishment after worshipping the calf: they were ordered to kill themselves or leave their homes, yet these addressees would not have obeyed except for a few.
rows.anchor: أي لو اوجبنا عليهم مثل ما أوجبنا على بني إسرائيل من قتلهم انفسهم أو خروجهم من ديارهم حين استتيبوا من عبادة العجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s ‘few’ is a strong rebuke; the nominative reading makes ‘few’ a substitute for the subject pronoun, while the accusative reading is ordinary exception or an adverbial ‘doing little.’
rows.anchor: وهذا توبيخ عظيم والرفع على البدل من الواو في ( فعلوه ) وقرىء ( إلا قليلا ) بالنصب على أصل الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What they are admonished to do is follow and obey the Messenger and submit to his judgment, since he is truthful and does not speak from desire.
rows.anchor: من اتباع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وطاعته والانقياد لما يراه ويحكم به لأنه الصادق المصدوق الذي لا ينطق عن الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obedience would benefit them in both their immediate life and the hereafter.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لكان خيرا لهم ﴾ في عاجلهم وآجلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It would strengthen their faith and keep them farther from wavering in it.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأشد تثبيتا ﴾ لايمانهم وأبعد من الاضطراب فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Then’ answers an implied question about what else they would receive after steadfastness: if they remained firm, God would grant more.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وإذا ﴾ جواب لسؤال مقدر كانه قيل وماذا يكون لهم أيضا بعد التثبيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘We would give them’ follows because ‘then’ functions as answer and consequence; the reward ‘from Us’ is a gracious gift, called reward because it follows their steadfast action.
rows.anchor: في ان لمراد العطاء المتفضل به من عنده وتسميته أجرا لأنه تابع للأجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘from Him’ in the parallel verse signals a gift bestowed by grace.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ويؤت من لدنه أجرا عظيما ﴾ 40 في ان لمراد العطاء المتفضل به من عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘We would guide them’ means God would show them kindness and grant success in increasing good deeds.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولهديناهم ﴾ وللطفنا بهم ووفقناهم لازدياد الخيرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ṣiddīqūn are the foremost companions of prophets, who preceded others in believing, like Abu Bakr, and were truthful in speech and action.
rows.anchor: الصديقون أفاضل صحابة الأنبياء الذين تقدموا في تصديقهم كابي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه وصدقوا في أقوالهم وأفعالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of companionship with God’s nearest and highest-ranking servants encourages believers to obey.
rows.anchor: وهذا ترغيب للمؤمنين في الطاعة حيث وعدوا مرافقة أقرب عباد الله إلى الله وأرفعهم درجات عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘How excellent those are as companions’ carries an exclamation of admiration; one reading has a sukun on the sīn, and the phrase may be parsed like adjectival exclamations with a fixed predicate.
rows.anchor: فيه معنى التعجب كانه قيل وماأحسن أولئك رفيقا لاستقلاله بمعنى التعجب قرىء ( وحسن ) بسكون السين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rafīq can function like ṣadīq or khalīṭ with the same form for singular and plural, or be singular while denoting a class in the specification construction.
rows.anchor: والرفيق كالصديق والخليط في استواء الواحد والجمع فيه ويجوز ان يكون مفردا بين به الجنس في باب التمييز

rows.speaker: ثوبان
rows.claim: Thawban’s intense love made him fear that his lower rank in Paradise would keep him from seeing the Prophet; the report says the verse was revealed after he expressed that fear.
rows.anchor: أن ثوبان مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان شديد الحب لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قليل الصبر عنه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet swore that a person’s faith is incomplete until he loves the Prophet more than himself, his parents, family, children, and all people.
rows.anchor: فقال يا رسول الله ما بي من وجع غير إني اذا لم أرك اشتقت اليك واستوحشت وحشة شديدة

rows.speaker: جماعة من الصحابة
rows.claim: The same account is also related about a group of Companions.
rows.anchor: وحكى ذلك عن جماعة من الصحابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, ‘that’ may be the subject, ‘the grace’ its modifier, and ‘from God’ the predicate; alternatively, ‘the grace is from God’ is the predicate of ‘that.’
rows.anchor: ﴿ ذلك ﴾ مبتدأ و ﴿ الفضل ﴾ صفته و ﴿ من الله ﴾ الخبر ويجوز ان يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great reward and companionship given to the obedient come from God as a gracious addition to their recompense.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أن ما اعطي المطيعون من الأجر العظيم ومرافقة المنعم عليهم من الله لأنه تفضل به عليهم تبعا لثوابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The excellence of those favored is from God because their achievement depends on His enabling and guidance; God knows His servants and gives success according to their circumstances.
rows.anchor: أو اراد ان فضل المنعم عليهم ومزيتهم من الله لأنهم اكتسبوه بتمكينه وتوفيقه وكفي بالله عليما بعباده فهو يوفقهم على حسب أحوالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shaʿāʾir are signs or markers of ritual: Hajj stations, places for stoning, the circumambulation and saʿy, and acts such as entering consecration, shaving, and sacrifice.
rows.anchor: الشعائر جمع شعيرة وهي اسم ما اشعر أي جعل شعارا وعلما للنسك من مواقف الحج ومرامي الجمار والمطاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘sacred month’ here is the month of Hajj.
rows.anchor: والشهر الحرام شهر الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hady is an offering sent to the House as a sacrifice; qalāʾid are the garlands put on such offerings, made from a sandal, waterskin strap, bark, or similar material.
rows.anchor: والهدي ما اهدي إلى البيت وتقرب به إلى الله من النسائك وهو جمع هدية كما يقال جدي في جمع جدية السرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those journeying to the Sacred House are pilgrims and people performing ʿumra.
rows.anchor: والقلائد جمع قلادة وهي ما قلد به الهدي من نعل أو عروة مزادة أو لحاء شجر أوغيره وآمو المسجد الحرام قاصدوه وهم الحجاج والعمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Violating these sanctities includes treating rites lightly, obstructing worshippers, creating barriers during Hajj, seizing the offerings, or preventing them from reaching their destination.
rows.anchor: وإحلال هذه الأشياء ان يتهاون بحرمة الشعائر وان يحال بينها وبين المتنسكين بها وان يحدثوا في أشهر الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation of ‘the garlands’ is the garlanded sacrificial camels; the wording singles them out for emphasis because they are the most noble offerings.
rows.anchor: اما القلائد ففيها وجهان أحدهما ان يراد بها ذوات القلائد من الهدي وهي البدن وتعطف على الهدي للاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first interpretation is like mentioning Gabriel and Michael specially: the garlanded offerings are singled out from the broader category for emphasis.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وجبريل وميكال ﴾ البقرة 98 كانه قيل والقلائد منها خصوصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation directly forbids interfering with the offerings’ garlands, intensifying the prohibition against interfering with the offerings themselves; it resembles forbidding display of adornment by forbidding its sites.
rows.anchor: والثاني ان ينهي عن التعرض لقلائد الهدي مبالغة في النهي عن التعرض للهدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Do not violate the month’ also means do not violate people heading to the Sacred Mosque; they seek reward from their Lord and His approval, so they should be honored and left unharmed.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولا الشهر ﴾ ولا تحلوا قوما قاصدين المسجد الحرام ﴿ يبتغون فضلا من ربهم ﴾ وهو الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some said this verse remains in force (muḥkama).
rows.anchor: أي لا تتعرضوا لقوم هذه صفتهم تعظيما لهم واستنكارا ان يتعرض لمثلهم قيل هي محكمة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A mursal report says al-Māʾida was among the last revelations and instructs people to permit its lawful things and forbid its unlawful ones.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan said that nothing in this sura is abrogated.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن ليس فيها منسوخ وعن أبي ميسرة فيها ثماني عشرة فريضة

rows.speaker: أبو ميسرة
rows.claim: Abu Maysara said the sura contains eighteen obligations and none is abrogated.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي ميسرة فيها ثماني عشرة فريضة وليس فيها منسوخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the verse is abrogated.
rows.anchor: وليس فيها منسوخ وقيل هي منسوخة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas said Muslims and polytheists had both performed Hajj, so God forbade Muslims from preventing anyone from visiting the House.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس كان المسلمون والمشركون يحجون جميعا فنهى الله المسلمين ان يمنعوا احدا عن حج البيت بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Ibn Abbas’s account, the prohibition on obstructing pilgrims was later followed by the commands that polytheists are impure and may not maintain God’s mosques.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لا تحلوا ﴾ ثم نزل بعد ذلك ﴿ إنما المشركون نجس ﴾ التوبة 28

rows.speaker: مجاهد والشعبي
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Shaʿbi held that ‘do not violate’ was abrogated by the command to fight them wherever they are found.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد والشعبي ﴿ لا تحلوا ﴾ نسخ بقوله ﴿ واقتلوهم حيث وجدتموهم ﴾ النساء 89

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God’s bounty means trade; seeking His approval describes the polytheists’ own belief that their religion was sound and pilgrimage brought them nearer to God.
rows.anchor: وفسر ابتغاء الفضل بالتجارة وابتغاء الرضوان بان المشركين كانوا يظنون في انفسهم أنهم على سداد من دينهم

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah read ‘and those aiming for the Sacred House’ with an iḍāfa construction.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله ( ولا أمي البيت الحرام ) على الاضافة

rows.speaker: حميد بن قيس والأعرج
rows.claim: Humayd ibn Qays and al-Aʿraj read ‘seeking’ in the second person, addressing the believers.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حميد بن قيس والأعرج ( تبتغون ) بالتاء على خطاب المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘When you leave consecration, then hunt’ permits hunting after it had been prohibited during consecration; the wording implies there is no blame in doing so.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فاصطادوا ﴾ إباحة للاصطياد بعد حظره عليهم كانه قيل وإذا حللتم فلا جناح عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading pronounces the fāʾ in ‘faṣṭādū’ with kasra; one explanation treats it as replacing the initial hamza’s kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بكسر الفاء وقيل هو بدل من كسر الهمزة عند الابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads ‘when you become lawful’; both ḥalla and aḥalla are used for leaving consecration.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( إذا أحللتم ) يقال حل المحرم وأحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: J-r-m behaves like k-s-b in taking one or two objects; the hamzated form transfers a one-object verb to two objects, as in akسبته, and Abdullah reads the hamzated form.
rows.anchor: ( جرم ) يجري مجرى ( كسب ) في تعديه إلى مفعول واحد واثنين تقول جرم ذنبا نحو كسبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa, ‘that they barred you’ is attached to ‘resentment’ as its cause; shanaʾān means intense hatred, and the sense is that hostility must not drive aggression.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أن تعتدوا ﴾ و ﴿ أن صدوكم ﴾ بفتح الهمزة متعلق بالشنآن بمعنى العلة والشنآن شدة البغض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word shanaʾān is also read with a sukūn on the nūn.
rows.anchor: والشنآن شدة البغض وقرىء بسكون النون والمعنى ولا يكسبنكم بغض قوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings make the phrase conditional: ‘if they barred you,’ or Abdullah’s ‘if they bar you.’
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( إن صدوكم ) على ( إن ) الشرطية وفي قراءة عبد الله ( إن يصدوكم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference is to Meccan pagans preventing the Prophet and believers from performing ʿumra at al-Hudaybiya; aggression means retaliating by inflicting harm.
rows.anchor: ومعنى صدهم إياهم عن المسجد الحرام منع اهل مكة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والمؤمنين يوم الحديبية عن العمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cooperating in righteousness and piety means forgiving and overlooking offenses.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وتعاونوا على البر والتقوى ﴾ على العفو والإغضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not cooperating in sin and aggression means refusing revenge and vindictiveness.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولا تعاونوا على الإثم والعدوان ﴾ على الانتقام والتشفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, both commands are general: they cover every good and pious act, every sin and aggression, and thus both forgiveness and retaliation.
rows.anchor: ويجوز ان يراد العموم لكل بر وتقوى وكل إثم وعدوان فيتناول بعمومه العفو والانتصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hunting command again is explained as permission after the ban of consecration ends.
rows.anchor: إباحة للاصطياد بعد حظره عليهم كانه قيل وإذا حللتم فلا جناح عليكم ان تصطادوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ is also read with kasra, explained as replacing the kasra of an initial hamza; another reading has ‘when you leave consecration.’
rows.anchor: وقرىء بكسر الفاء وقيل هو بدل من كسر الهمزة عند الابتداء وقرىء ( إذا أحللتم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: J-r-m follows k-s-b in taking one or two objects; its hamzated form adds a second object, and Abdullah reads it with the hamza prefix.
rows.anchor: ( جرم ) يجري مجرى ( كسب ) في تعديه إلى مفعول واحد واثنين تقول جرم ذنبا نحو كسبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa, ‘that they barred you’ is attached to ‘resentment’ as its cause; shanaʾān means intense hatred, and the sense is that hostility must not drive aggression.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أن تعتدوا ﴾ و ﴿ أن صدوكم ﴾ بفتح الهمزة متعلق بالشنآن بمعنى العلة والشنآن شدة البغض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word shanaʾān is also read with a sukūn on the nūn.
rows.anchor: والشنآن شدة البغض وقرىء بسكون النون والمعنى ولا يكسبنكم بغض قوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings make the phrase conditional: ‘if they barred you,’ or Abdullah’s ‘if they bar you.’
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( إن صدوكم ) على ( إن ) الشرطية وفي قراءة عبد الله ( إن يصدوكم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference is to Meccan pagans preventing the Prophet and believers from performing ʿumra at al-Hudaybiya; aggression means retaliating by inflicting harm.
rows.anchor: ومعنى صدهم عن المسجد الحرام منع اهل مكة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والمؤمنين يوم الحديبية عن العمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cooperating in righteousness and piety means forgiving and overlooking offenses.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وتعاونوا على البر والتقوى ﴾ على العفو والإغضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not cooperating in sin and aggression means refusing revenge and vindictiveness.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولا تعاونوا على الإثم والعدوان ﴾ على الانتقام والتشفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, both commands are general: they cover every good and pious act, every sin and aggression, and thus both forgiveness and retaliation.
rows.anchor: ويجوز ان يراد العموم لكل بر وتقوى وكل إثم وعدوان فيتناول بعمومه العفو والانتصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indirect question means ‘they say to you, what has been made lawful for them’; the shift to third person follows the wording ‘they ask you,’ though first person would also be correct.
rows.anchor: في السؤال معنى القول فلذلك وقع بعده ﴿ ماذا أحل لهم ﴾ كأنه قيل يقولون لك ماذا احل لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘What’ is the subject and ‘has been made lawful for them’ its predicate; the question concerns foods after prohibited foods were recited to them.
rows.anchor: و ( ماذا ) مبتدأ وأحل لهم ) خبره كقولك أي شيء احل لهم ومعناه ماذا احل لهم من المطاعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Good things’ means what is not foul: anything not prohibited by scripture, the Sunna, or a jurist’s analogy.
rows.anchor: أي ما ليس بخبيث منها وهو كل ما لم يات تحريمه في كتاب أو سنة أو قياس مجتهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trained hunting animals may coordinate with ‘good things’ with an omitted word, meaning lawful food and game caught by your trained animals; alternatively, ‘what’ is conditional and ‘eat’ is its answer.
rows.anchor: عطف على الطيبات أي أحل لكم الطيبات وصيد ما علمتم فحذف المضاف أو تجعل ( ما ) شرطية وجوابها ( فكلوا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jawāriḥ are hunting predators among beasts and birds, including dogs, leopards, tigers, eagles, falcons, and hawks.
rows.anchor: والجوارح الكواسب من سباع البهائم والطير كالكلب والفهد والنمر والعقاب والصقر والبازي والشاهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukallib is the person who trains and disciplines hunting animals for their owner; the word derives from dogs because dogs are the most common, or because predators are called dogs.
rows.anchor: والمكلب مؤدب الجوارح ومضربها بالصيد لصاحبها ورائضها لذلك بما علم من الحيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term can also derive from a predator being called a dog, or from keliba, ‘to be keenly attached’ to something.
rows.anchor: أو لأن السبع يسمى كلبا ومنه قوله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To show that a predator is called a dog, the author cites a Prophetic supplication for God to set one of His dogs on a man; the animal was a lion.
rows.anchor: اللهم سلط عليه كلبا من كلابك ) + + فأكله الأسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word can also mean keenly attached to something, as in describing someone as ‘a dog’ for it.
rows.anchor: أو من الكلب الذي هو بمعنى الضراوة يقال هو كلب بكذا اذا كان ضاريا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Trainers’ is a circumstantial accusative modifying ‘you have trained’; it indicates a highly skilled expert in training hunting animals.
rows.anchor: فائدتها ان يكون من يعلم الجوارح نحريرا في علمه مدربا فيه موصوفا بالتكليب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Teaching them’ is either a second circumstantial clause or a new sentence; the verse teaches that learners should seek knowledge from the most expert and discerning teachers, even over long journeys.
rows.anchor: و ﴿ تعلمونهن ﴾ حال ثانية أو استئناف وفيه فائدة جليلة وهي ان على كل آخذ علما ان لا يأخذه الا من أقتل اهله علما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God taught means the knowledge of training, divinely inspired yet acquired through reason; alternatively it is what God showed people about sending, recalling, stopping, and retaining the catch for its owner.
rows.anchor: ﴿ مما علمكم الله ﴾ من علم التكليب لأنه الهام من الله ومكتسب بالعقل أو مما عرفكم ان تعلموه من اتباع الصيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads mukallibīn with a lighter form; afʿala and faʿʿala often share a meaning.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( مكلبين ) بالتخفيف وأفعل وفعل يشتركان كثيرا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a sound report to ʿAdi ibn Hatim, the Prophet says not to eat the catch if the dog ate it, since it caught for itself.
rows.anchor: لقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام لعدي بن حاتم

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali said not to eat the catch if a falcon ate from it.
rows.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه إذا اكل البازي فلا تاكل

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Scholars differed: some require predatory beasts to refrain from eating because they can be trained by beating, but do not impose the condition on predatory birds.
rows.anchor: وفرق العلماء فاشترطوا في سباع البهائم ترك الأكل لأنها تؤدب بالضرب ولم يشترطوه في سباع الطير

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars do not treat eating as relevant and do not distinguish an animal holding all of the prey from holding only part.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من لم يعتبر ترك الأكل أصلا ولم يفرق بين إمساك الكل والبعض

rows.speaker: سلمان وسعد بن أبي وقاص وأبو هريرة
rows.claim: Salman, Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas, and Abu Hurayra allowed eating when a dog consumed two-thirds, left one-third, and God’s name had been invoked.
rows.anchor: وعن سلمان وسعد بن أبي وقاص وأبي هريرة رضي الله عنهم اذا اكل الكلب ثلثيه وبقي ثلثه وذكرت اسم الله عليه فكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ‘mention God’s name over it’ can refer to the catch: invoke God when you find it alive and slaughter it.
rows.anchor: قلت إما ان يرجع إلى ما أمسكن على معنى وسموا عليه إذا ادركتم ذكاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to the trained animal, so God’s name is invoked when it is sent out.
rows.anchor: أو إلى ما علمتم من الجوارح أي سموا عليه عند إرساله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says a group of Jews asked the Prophet which messengers he believed in; when they heard him mention Jesus, they insulted the Muslims’ religion, and the verse was revealed. The author grades the report weak.
rows.anchor: أنه اتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نفر من اليهود فسالوه عمن يؤمن به من الرسل فقال

rows.speaker: نعيم بن ميسرة
rows.claim: Nuʿaym ibn Maysara read ‘and most of you’ with kasra on the hamza.
rows.anchor: وعن نعيم بن ميسرة ( وإن أكثركم ) بالكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘That most of you’ may be accusative after an implied verb indicated by ‘do you resent,’ or nominative with an omitted predicate: your transgression is established, since you know the Muslims are right but leadership and wealth prevent fairness.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل ان ينتصب ( وأن أكثركم ) بفعل محذوف يدل عليه هل تنقمون أي ولا تنقمون ان اكثركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘That’ points to what is resented; a genitive phrase must be supplied before ‘that’ or before ‘who,’ such as ‘people of that’ or ‘a religion of those whom God cursed.’
rows.anchor: ﴿ ذلك ﴾ إشارة إلى المنقوم ولا بد من حذف مضاف قبله أو قبل ( من ) تقديره بشر من أهل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Those whom God cursed’ can be nominative as an identification (‘he is one of those’) or genitive as an appositive to ‘worse.’
rows.anchor: ﴿ من لعنه الله ﴾ في محل الرفع على قولك هو من لعنه الله كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two readings mathūba and mathūba follow the forms of mashūra and mashūra; ‘reward’ is used for punishment as a rhetorical inversion, like calling a painful blow a greeting.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( مثوبة ) ( ومثوبة ) ومثالهما مشورة ومشورة فإن قلت المثوبة مختصة بالإحسان فكيف جاءت في الإساءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same inversion appears in ‘give them good news of painful punishment.’
rows.anchor: ومنه ﴿ فبشرهم بعذاب أليم ﴾ آل عمران 21

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two parties share the punishment in the Jews’ accusation: they claim Muslims are astray and deserve punishment, so those cursed by God are worse in reality than Muslims are in the Jews’ claim.
rows.anchor: كان اليهود لعنوا يزعمون أن المسلمين ضالون مستوجبون للعقاب فقيل لهم من لعنه الله شر عقوبة في الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘and worshipped the false deity’ is joined to the relative clause; Ubayy read ‘and they worshipped,’ and Ibn Masʿud read ‘and those who worshipped.’
rows.anchor: ﴿ وعبد الطاغوت ﴾ عطف على صلة ( من ) كانه قيل ومن عبد الطاغوت وفي قراءة أبي ( وعبدوا الطاغوت )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings include ‘worshipper of the false deity,’ ‘worshippers,’ and forms in which the word means excessive devotion; the accompanying poetry illustrates ʿabd as an emphatic description of servitude.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( وعابد الطاغوت ) عطفا على القردة ( وعابدي ) ( وعباد ) ( وعبد ) ( وعبد ) ومعناه الغلو في العبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also explains the various forms morphologically: ʿabd on the ḥuṭam pattern, ʿabīd/ʿabd as plurals, and forms related to ʿabada, khadam, and ʿābid.
rows.anchor: وعبد بوزن حطم وعبيد وعبد بضمتين جمع عبيد وعبدة بوزن كفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some vocalizations are passive with an omitted pronoun, meaning the false deity was worshipped among them; another means that the false deity became an object of worship, like amara meaning ‘became a ruler.’
rows.anchor: وعبد الطاغوت على البناء للمفعول وحذف الراجع بمعنى وعبد الطاغوت فيهم أو بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asked how God could make them worship false deities, the author gives two explanations: God abandoned them until they worshipped, or He judged and described them that way.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت كيف جاز ان يجعل الله منهم عباد الطاغوت قلت فيه وجهان أحدهما انه خذلهم حتى عبدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second explanation is like the statement that they made angels, servants of the Merciful, female; the author links it to 43:19.
rows.anchor: والثاني أنه حكم عليهم بذلك ووصفهم به كقوله تعالى ﴿ وجعلوا الملائكة الذين هم عباد الرحمن إناثا ﴾ الزخرف 19

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some said the false deity is the calf: worshipping it, which Satan adorned for them, amounts to worshipping Satan, the false deity.
rows.anchor: وقيل الطاغوت العجل لأنه معبود من دون الله ولأن عبادتهم للعجل مما زينه لهم الشيطان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas said they obeyed soothsayers; anyone obeyed in disobedience to God is thereby worshipped.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه أطاعوا الكهنة وكل من اطاع احدا في معصية الله فقد عبده

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan read the plural form ṭawāghīt.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( الطواغيت )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view assigns the apes to the People of the Sabbath and the pigs to the unbelievers associated with Jesus’ table; another says both forms of metamorphosis befell the People of the Sabbath, with young men turned to apes and elders to pigs.
rows.anchor: وقيل وجعل منهم القردة أصحاب السبت والخنازير كفار أهل مائدة عيسى وقيل كلا المسخين من أصحاب السبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that after revelation Muslims mocked Jews as ‘brothers of apes and pigs,’ and the Jews lowered their heads.
rows.anchor: وروي انها لما نزلت كان المسلمون يعيرون اليهود ويقولون يا اخوة القردة والخنازير فينكسون رءوسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Those’ refers to the accursed and transformed people.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أولئك ﴾ الملعونون الممسوخون
